review_notes: I read the whole file. I checked intAlgHom against Mathlib's RingHom.toIntAlgHom and grepped the repo, where intAlgHom is redefined in about 11 files. I also looked at the other candidates: castPar, ιO (a matrix-based base change between Module.End ℤ and Module.End 𝒪 of different modules), κ, Λ₀, χ₀ and resO. None of these has a clear Mathlib counterpart, so I did not report them. The remaining uncertainty is whether the generic Algebra ℤ instance argument in intAlgHom would cause instance-mismatch problems when switching to the Mathlib version. All concrete types used here (End, tensor product, heckeAlgebra subring, field) are Rings with the canonical ℤ-algebra structure, so I expect it to work. I did not compile anything.

findings.problem: intAlgHom reinterprets a ring homomorphism as a ℤ-algebra homomorphism. Mathlib already has this as RingHom.toIntAlgHom, which comes with the simp lemma toIntAlgHom_coe and the lemma toIntAlgHom_apply. Both constructions are `{ f with commutes' := ... }`. The local version is also copied into about eleven other files under P2M/Sol, so there are many competing local copies. Their signatures differ (Semiring vs Ring, Type vs Type*, a CommRing variant with `{_ : Algebra ℤ A}`). Every use here is at Ring types: End, a tensor product, the heckeAlgebra subring and a field.
findings.proposed_change: Delete intAlgHom and intAlgHom_apply. Use `(ιO N 𝒪 bZ bO).toIntAlgHom`, `((ιO N 𝒪 bZ bO).comp ρ).toIntAlgHom`, `θ.toIntAlgHom` and `ρ.toIntAlgHom` at lines 167, 213, 222, 225, 230 and 258. Replace `intAlgHom_apply` in the rewrite at line 225 with `RingHom.toIntAlgHom_apply`. Alternatively, if Semiring generality is really needed, put one generalized version in the shared P2M.Util and have the other files import it.
findings.benefit: Removes a duplicate of a Mathlib definition and the repeated per-file copies. Readers meet the standard name and its simp API, and results can be combined with other Mathlib code that uses toIntAlgHom without conversions.
